historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is undefined -- shareholders' equity has been negative since FY2022 due to cumulative debt-funded share buybacks, not distress (net debt/EBITDA remains ~1.1x, investment grade). Equity CAGR is therefore NOT usable as the primary growth anchor (contrary to the default logic in Step 1c); revenue CAGR is used instead as the conservative, best-available anchor, cross-checked against FY2027 segment guidance (blended ~4.2%) and management's medium-term Specialty/MSO growth narrative. EPS CAGR (78.9%/3yr) is heavily distorted by the FY2023 EPS trough ($1.27, itself depressed by opioid litigation charges) and buyback-driven share count decline (~3.3%/yr) -- not used as an anchor. FCF 3yr CAGR (24.2%, reported basis) is inflated by FY2026's one-off working-capital swing and tariff refund; the owner-FCF component build in this file does not extrapolate that rate.

scenario_narratives.base: Cardinal Health continues as one of the 'Big Three' US pharmaceutical distributors (>90% combined share with McKesson and Cencora), growing revenue at a mid-single-digit rate driven by drug-price inflation and Specialty/biologic mix in the ~92%-of-revenue Pharma segment, while the small but fast-growing MSO and Specialty-adjacent 'Other' segment (currently ~3% of revenue, guided 11-13% growth) gradually lifts the blended margin. EBITDA margin keeps climbing off its FY2022 trough (0.05%) toward a mature ~1.65%, but FY2026's outsized 91% GMPD profit surge (largely a one-time ~$100M tariff refund) does not repeat, and FY2027's own guidance already calls for GMPD profit to fall and adjusted FCF to normalize down from $5.0B to $3.5-4.0B.
scenario_narratives.bull: The fragmented physician-practice market in GI, urology and oncology consolidates onto Cardinal's Specialty Alliance MSO platforms faster than guided, Specialty/BioPharma (including radiopharmacy) sustains its 30%+ growth rate for longer, and GMPD's improvement plan produces durable (not just tariff-refund-driven) margin gains -- compounding into materially higher EBITDA margins and growth than the core distribution business alone would support.
scenario_narratives.bear: IRA Medicare drug-price negotiation expands into more Part D drugs in 2027 and Part B drugs in 2028, compressing the already-thin (3-4% gross margin) core distribution economics on a growing share of branded volume; unresolved 340B contract-pharmacy disputes add further uncertainty; the rapid, debt- and cash-funded MSO acquisition spree (GI Alliance, Solaris, ADS, ION -- several billion dollars in under two years) proves harder to integrate than guided; and GMPD's FY2026 profit surge reverses fully once the one-time tariff refund rolls off, with no offsetting structural improvement.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cardinal Health is valued on a standard owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted across bear/base/bull, using a 10-year explicit horizon because the component-built EBITDA margin (1.40% FY2026 actual, climbing toward a projected ~1.65% mature level) has not yet matured by year 5. The business is a genuine high-volume, low-margin logistics/distribution operation -- gross margins of 3-4% and EBITDA margins near 1.4% are structural, not depressed, and the model does NOT extrapolate margin expansion beyond what the disclosed segment mix shift (Specialty/BioPharma growth, MSO physician-practice platforms, GMPD's improvement plan) plausibly supports; FY2026's outsized 91% GMPD profit growth and its own guided FY2027 step-down in adjusted free cash flow ($5.0B to $3.5-4.0B) are both treated as evidence AGAINST extrapolating the most recent year's results, not as a new steady state. SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charged once) and the share count held flat rather than compounded with the historical ~3%/yr buyback-driven decline, since the buybacks are the mechanism funding the flat count, not a source of incremental per-share value on top of it. Net debt (not net cash) means no interest-income strip applies. The largest unresolved modeling simplification is noncontrolling interests in the majority-owned MSO platforms (GI Alliance ~73%, Solaris/Specialty Alliance ~76%): the consolidated EBIT/EBITDA build is not adjusted for NCI because no NCI figure is disclosed in the parsed data, but the 'Other' segment containing the MSOs is still only ~3% of revenue today, so the resulting overstatement of shareholder value is small at current scale and will need revisiting if MSO scaling accelerates as guided (11-13% segment growth).
key_risks_to_valuation: IRA Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program expansion (more Part D drugs in 2027, Part B drugs in 2028) compressing already-thin core distribution margins on a growing share of branded volume
Unresolved 340B contract-pharmacy disputes creating multi-year uncertainty on distribution volumes and rebate economics

MSO integration risk from four billion-dollar-plus acquisitions (GI Alliance, Solaris Health, Advanced Diabetes Supply, ION) completed in under two years, in a business model distinct from core distribution
Customer concentration: a small number of very large customers (CVS Health, OptumRx, major GPOs) represent an outsized share of revenue and receivables
Legacy opioid litigation exposure (ongoing settlement obligations)

GMPD segment profit is guided to fall in FY2027 as the one-time ~$100M IEEPA tariff refund rolls off -- if the underlying improvement-plan progress is weaker than assumed, margin could fall further than modeled
NCI in majority-owned (not wholly-owned) MSO platforms is not separately deducted in this build; a scale-up of the MSO segment without a corresponding NCI adjustment would overstate per-share value

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 149.6-258.3
data_sources.financials: CAH_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL-derived, 103 periods FY2007-FY2026) and dcf_context.py KPI pivot (buybacks, cash_taxes, ebitda_da)
data_sources.qualitative: CAH_Analysis.json (business_model, competitive_position, growth_drivers, risks, guidance, bull_case, bear_case), analysis dated for Q4/FY2026 earnings release (August 2026) and FY2027 guidance

inputs.sbc_source: CAH_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2026 (SEC XBRL cash-flow-statement SBC add-back); no separate equity-award-tax-withholding line disclosed in a combined reconciliation figure -- used as-is; net debt is positive (total debt $8,886M > cash $4,856M), so no interest-income strip applies
inputs.wacc_rationale: US risk-free ~4.2% (10yr UST) + ERP ~5.0% x levered beta ~0.85-0.95 for a low-cyclicality, investment-grade distributor with moderate net debt (~1.1x EBITDA) => cost of equity ~8.5-9.0%; blended with a modest after-tax cost of debt on ~$8.9B of investment-grade debt gives WACC ~7.5%. Rounded WACC=7.5% for base case.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are not disclosed as a material component of CAH's cost structure or debt stack in the extracted filings (distribution/logistics real estate is a small fraction of a $254B-revenue business); no separate lease adjustment applied. Total debt figure used is the reported CSV TotalDebt (bonds/notes), and no lease liability add-back or principal deduction is made.
inputs.nci_treatment: CAH consolidates majority-owned MSO platforms (GI Alliance ~73%, Solaris Health/The Specialty Alliance ~76%) with noncontrolling interests. NCI is not broken out as a separate line in the parsed CSV/KPI data (no dedicated NCI column disclosed), and the 'Other' segment containing the MSOs is only ~3% of FY2026 revenue (growing toward higher single digits under guidance). The EBIT/EBITDA build here is on a consolidated (pre-NCI-deduction) basis, consistent with reported NetIncome including NCI attribution embedded in the same CSV NetIncome figure; this slightly overstates value attributable to CAH shareholders as the MSO platforms scale, but the effect is second-order at current segment mix (~3% of revenue) and is flagged here rather than modeled explicitly for lack of a disclosed NCI split.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted, per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/references/owner-fcf.md -- CAH is a standard US operating company (pharmaceutical/medical distributor), not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco/distressed shell, so no special model applies. 10-year horizon used because the component-built EBITDA margin is still ramping (1.40% FY26 actual -> ~1.65% mature) and has not matured by year 5 (checklist section 2d). Net debt (not net cash) means no interest-income strip is needed -- CAH has no material interest income to double-count. Shareholders' equity is deeply negative (-$2.9B) purely from a decade of buybacks funded by debt-financed and cash-generative operations; this is a capital-structure choice, not a distress signal, and is explicitly NOT used as the historical-growth anchor (equity CAGR is undefined/meaningless on a negative base) -- revenue CAGR is used instead, cross-checked against FY2027 segment-level guidance. FY2026's reported FCF ($4,525M, 1.78% of revenue) was inflated by a large one-off working-capital swing (~$1.9B versus the EBIT-implied run rate) and a ~$100M one-time GMPD tariff refund; management's own FY2027 guidance for adjusted FCF ($3.5-4.0B, down from $5.0B) confirms this is not repeatable, so the forward build uses the EBITDA-margin/capex/tax component path (section 2) rather than carrying FY2026's elevated FCF conversion forward. Working-capital capture is modeled as a small POSITIVE capture on revenue growth (unusual for a distributor) because CAH's own multi-year OCF-less-capex-versus-EBIT relationship shows working capital has historically been a mild net source of cash on growth (large customers pay on favorable terms; CAH extends manufacturer payables), not a drag -- captured conservatively at a rate well below the noisy historical average (which is distorted by opioid-litigation charges embedded in several years' operating income). Cash tax rate is ramped from FY2026's unusually low ~12.9% (on EBIT) toward the company's own guided effective rate of 19-20% (using 21% mature) over 5 years, since the gap looks like a timing/NOL benefit rather than a sustainable rate. Buybacks ($1,358M in FY2026, consistent with ~$1B/yr guided for FY2027) are the funding mechanism for the flat share count; SBC is fully expensed in the flows per section 1, so annual_share_growth_pct=0 and the count is held flat rather than compounding the recent 3%/yr buyback-driven share count decline (which would double-count the SBC charge).

bear.narrative: Bear case: Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program (IRA) expansion into more Part D drugs (2027) and Part B drugs (2028), combined with unresolved 340B contract-pharmacy disputes, compresses core distribution economics on a growing share of branded volume just as GMPD loses its one-time tariff-refund tailwind. MSO integration (GI Alliance, Solaris, ION -- several billion dollars deployed in under two years) proves harder than expected, diverting management attention and capital without the guided profit growth. A major customer (CVS Health or OptumRx) renegotiates or reduces its distribution relationship. Opioid litigation produces a new adverse ruling or settlement. Margins stall near the historical mid-cycle level rather than continuing to climb.

base.narrative: Base case: FY2027 revenue growth ~4.5%, near the blended segment guidance midpoint (~4.2%: Pharma 3-5%, GMPD 2-4%, Other/MSO 11-13%), decelerating gently to a 2.5% terminal rate as Specialty and MSO scaling continues to lift the mix but the core Pharma distribution business (still ~92% of revenue) stays a low-single-digit-growth, price-driven business. EBITDA margin continues its multi-year climb (0.05% FY22 trough to 1.40% FY26) toward a mature ~1.65%, reflecting continued Specialty/BioPharma mix shift and MSO platform scaling, but GMPD's FY2026 profit surge (91% YoY, aided by a one-time ~$100M tariff refund) is NOT assumed to repeat -- FY2027 GMPD segment profit is guided DOWN. Cash tax rate ramps from FY2026's unusually low ~12.9% toward the company's own guided 19-20% effective range (21% mature) over 5 years.

bull.narrative: Bull case: MSO platform expansion (GI Alliance, Solaris Health/Urology, ION oncology) executes faster and more profitably than guided, the fragmented GI/urology physician-practice market (80-90% unaffiliated) consolidates onto Cardinal's platforms at pace, Specialty/BioPharma growth exceeds the 30%+ FY2026 rate for longer, and GMPD's improvement plan delivers structural (not just one-off tariff-driven) margin gains. Oligopoly pricing discipline among the Big Three distributors holds, letting margin gains flow through without competitive erosion.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default shifted slightly toward bear (20% vs the 15% default) given the specific, dated regulatory catalyst (IRA Medicare price negotiation expanding into more drugs in 2027 and Part B in 2028) plus the unusually rapid pace of debt/cash-funded MSO M&A (four billion-dollar-plus deals in under two years) that has not yet been tested through a full integration cycle. Bull weight held at 30% (below the 35% default) because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously -- MSO consolidation pace, sustained 30%+ Specialty/BioPharma growth, and durable (not tariff-driven) GMPD margin gains -- rather than a single lever.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
